clue.text: Currency in Europe's obsolete

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A remark that some former European money is no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers you to the old pre-euro currencies; the answer is spanning Europe's obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the monetary unit of Mexico and several other Latin American countries.

clue.text: Party held in check, closer?

indicators.note: something held in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a crew is a party or gang of people
to check something is to stop it

explanation.surface: A political party kept in check, perhaps nearing the close of its campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' is read as one who closes, not as nearer, and 'Party' is a gang rather than a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw top is a lid that twists shut, so it is something that closes a bottle or jar.

clue.text: Very exciting tomorrow, something Rishi deprived of?

blocks.note: the puzzle ran on Thursday 4 July 2024, election day, so tomorrow was Friday, abbreviated Fri
Rishi Sunak said in a campaign interview that he went without Sky TV as a child

explanation.surface: A jibe that the day after the election will be thrilling, and something Rishi Sunak once claimed to have gone without.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the British satellite TV service; Sunak's claim to have grown up without it was widely mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means lively and playful, a loose synonym for exciting or high-spirited.

clue.text: Tomorrow's headache, Matt? Member gone and Michael too – Labour's back!

indicators.note: something gone is taken away, so that part is dropped from the name before it
the back of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: Matt Hancock, the former Conservative health secretary
a vulgar word for the male member
Michael Gove, Conservative cabinet minister who stood down at the 2024 election
the final letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Election-night gloom for the Tories: Hancock and Gove are gone, and Labour has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the member out of HANCOCK, then add GOVE and the last letter of Labour to get HANGOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the headache that follows a night of drinking, here the day after election night.

clue.text: What things can only get for Rishi's campaign official?

blocks.note: first meaning: 'Things Can Only Get ...' was Labour's 1997 campaign anthem
second meaning: one who bets, as some Conservative campaign staff were found to have bet on the election date

explanation.walkthrough: The 2024 campaign had a scandal over Tory aides placing bets on when the election would be called, so the official is a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of good, completing the song title, and a noun for a person who places wagers.

clue.text: Rishi, say, tax-cutting leader of Opposition?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, the one kept here
a letter cutting into a word sits within it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: to tax someone's patience is to try it
the opening letter of Opposition

explanation.surface: A question whether Rishi Sunak will be the tax-cutting Leader of the Opposition after the election.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes into TRY. 'Leader of Opposition' looks like the parliamentary title but just gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunak was the Conservative leader, and Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.

clue.text: Something toxic with Plaid Cymru, and Liz Trussed?

indicators.note: plaid is a tartan cloth, criss-crossed, so the word beside it is woven into a new order
something trussed is bound up inside a wrapping, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Something poisonous involving the Welsh nationalist party Plaid Cymru and former PM Liz Truss.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party, but 'Plaid' is the tartan anagram signal, and 'Trussed' puns on former PM Liz Truss.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is a heavy metal whose vapour and compounds are poisonous.

clue.text: Country dispensing with old Conservative PM?

indicators.note: dispensing with something means doing without it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: the West African nation
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Asking which nation has given up on its former Conservative prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one O from CAMEROON. 'Old' looks attached to the PM but is the letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron led the Conservative Party and was UK prime minister from 2010 to 2016.

clue.text: Fossil fuel, Rishi's confessed addiction

blocks.note: first meaning: the solid fuel made by heating coal
second meaning: Sunak has admitted to being hooked on Coca-Cola

explanation.walkthrough: 'Confessed addiction' hints at the drug, but Sunak's admitted habit was the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is both a coal-derived fuel and the short name for Coca-Cola, which Sunak called his vice.

clue.text: Looking to the left, further thought surely vital

indicators.note: facing leftward means reading backwards, against the normal direction of English text

blocks.note: a postscript adds a further thought to a letter
rightly, as in 'surely so', with certainty

explanation.surface: A voter leaning left, adding that surely it is a vital point.
explanation.walkthrough: The left-versus-right politics of the surface hides the turnaround: 'Looking to the left' means read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy, which is what vital can mean.

clue.text: Reform tries to react, sending those coming in away – certainly not my cup of tea!

definitions.text: certainly not my cup of tea!

indicators.note: the inner letters are dispatched, leaving only the two at the outside of the word
to reform is to form again, rebuilding the letters in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of react

explanation.surface: Reform UK trying to respond by deporting immigrants, a policy the setter does not care for.
explanation.walkthrough: Reform UK is Nigel Farage's party with a hard line on immigration. The definition is playful: a ristretto is coffee, so literally not tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ristretto is a very short, concentrated espresso, a coffee rather than a cup of tea.

clue.text: Mean Conservative, shabby, premier to go?

indicators.note: the premier is the first in line, and it departs, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
tatty means worn and shabby

explanation.surface: A spiteful remark about a scruffy Tory whose prime minister must go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' suggests the PM but means the first letter of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty means spiteful or malicious in speech, a sense of mean as unkind.

clue.text: 6 party, flat

blocks.note: the answer to 6 is TORY, and Con is the short form of Conservative
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Tory party held in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to a Tory; CON stands in for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A condo, short for condominium, is an apartment in a building of individually owned units.

clue.text: Needing regeneration, Reeves leading the way – it's most brutal

indicators.note: regeneration rebuilds something from its parts, so the name is remade in another order
leading means going in front, so the rebuilt name comes before the next piece

blocks.note: Rachel Reeves, Labour's shadow chancellor in 2024
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Rachel Reeves taking the lead on economic regeneration, with spending cuts at their harshest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' tells you the shuffled name comes before ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest is the superlative of severe, meaning harshest, so it fits brutal in its most extreme form.

clue.text: Knack lost by leader on the hustings – tribal language?

indicators.note: something lost by a person is no longer with them, so that sound is taken away
the hustings are where candidates make speeches, so this works by sound

blocks.note: Rishi Sunak, the Conservative leader in 2024
say the leader's surname as 'Sue-nack' and drop the 'nack' sound

explanation.surface: A party leader losing his touch on the campaign trail.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunak spoken aloud is 'Sue' plus 'knack'; lose the knack and 'Sue' remains, spelt as the tribe's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sioux is a family of Native American languages spoken by the Lakota, Dakota and related peoples.

clue.text: Party seeking Independence Day to wrap up a kind of election

indicators.note: wrapping something up encloses it, so the party's letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: the Scottish National Party wants a day of independence for Scotland
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Scottish nationalists hoping an election will bring Scotland its independence day.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes inside SNP.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap election is one called suddenly, earlier than expected, as the 2024 UK election was.

clue.text: Horrifying thing not having capital for nurse

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, and here it is missing

blocks.note: something that frightens is a scarer

explanation.surface: A frightening prospect: no money for nursing care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but means the opening letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone sick or disabled, as a nurse does.

clue.text: Offensive plugging wind – what's the alternative?

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so this piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: rude means offensive or vulgar
to wind something is to coil it

explanation.surface: A rude remark promoting wind power, met with the question of what else would do.
explanation.walkthrough: RUDE goes into COIL. 'Wind' reads as wind power; its other sense, to coil, supplies the letters, and crude oil is the fossil alternative to wind energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrefined petroleum is the fossil-fuel alternative that wind power is meant to replace.

clue.text: Foot in door with pained expression, might one be slated?

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its bottom or final letter, the one kept

blocks.note: the final letter of door
oof is what you say when hurt or winded

explanation.surface: A canvasser getting a foot in the door and a groan, wondering if they'll be slated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slated' suggests criticised; here it means covered with slates.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofs are commonly covered with slate tiles, so a roof is a thing that gets slated.

clue.text: Astronomical effect in swing towards Labour?

blocks.note: first meaning: the stretching of light from receding galaxies to longer wavelengths
second meaning: a move by voters to the party whose colour is red

explanation.walkthrough: 'Astronomical' also suggests a huge swing, which the 2024 landslide was.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is Labour's party colour, so a shift to red is a swing to Labour, and the same phrase names the physics effect.

clue.text: Politician snarky in speech?

indicators.note: spoken words are heard rather than read, so this works by sound

blocks.note: mordant means sharply sarcastic or biting

explanation.surface: A politician being sarcastic in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny Mordaunt is a Conservative politician who lost her seat at the 2024 election.

clue.text: Rayner's moral responsibility with record investment?

indicators.note: investing something means putting it inside, here placing one piece within the other

blocks.note: a duty is a moral obligation
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Angela Rayner's sense of moral duty, alongside investment in the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rayner's' is read as 'Rayner is', so the name alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela Rayner was Labour's deputy leader, so she is a deputy, a second-in-command.

clue.text: Shower elected, given keys to number ten

blocks.note: a candidate who is elected is in
D and E are musical keys
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A useless lot elected and handed the keys to Number Ten Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' is a British insult for a useless bunch; here it is one who shows, and Number Ten, the PM's residence, is just X.
explanation.definitionFit: An index is a pointer or indicator, something that shows where things are.

clue.text: Brainwash, throwing up a little corporal: it's Nigel!

indicators.note: only a small part of the words is wanted, a run of letters inside them
in a down entry, thrown up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of corporal through the start of Nigel

explanation.surface: A disgusted reaction to a little corporal's propaganda, revealed as Nigel Farage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little corporal' was Napoleon's nickname, and Nigel is Farage; the reversed run gives INSTIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to fix it gradually in someone's mind, close to indoctrination.

clue.text: On two wings, Tories and DUP labouring

indicators.note: labouring means working hard, and worked letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The Tories and the DUP, both on the right wing, struggling at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labouring' teases the Labour party but just shuffles the letters. 'Two wings' suggests political wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipterous describes true flies, insects of the order Diptera, which have a single pair of wings.

clue.text: When party leader took eve off?

indicators.note: with 'off' later, to take something off is to remove it from the name
completes 'took off', signalling letters stripped out of the leader's name

blocks.note: Ed Davey, leader of the Liberal Democrats
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking when a party leader skipped the evening's events, recalling Sunak leaving the D-Day commemorations early.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E, V and E from ED DAVEY. Davey also made headlines in 2024 with campaign stunts like falling off a paddleboard.
explanation.definitionFit: D-Day is the date of the 1944 Normandy landings, and more generally the day something is set to happen.

clue.text: Trench dug, yah boo sucks!

blocks.note: first meaning: a sunken ditch serving as a fence in a landscaped garden
second meaning: a mocking laugh

explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a ditch with a wall on one side, keeping livestock out without blocking the view. 'Yah boo sucks' is British playground taunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a garden ditch-barrier and a jeering laugh at someone's misfortune.

clue.text: Debt: remove lid from jar

indicators.note: the lid is the top, which in a down entry is the first letter, taken away

blocks.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: An instruction to open a jar, under a heading about debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container to open, but it is a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in hock is to be in debt, or to have pawned something, so hock stands for debt.

clue.text: Leader befitting in marked man?

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits within it

blocks.note: apt means suitable or befitting
in Genesis, God put a mark on Cain after he killed Abel

explanation.surface: A leader worthy of a man singled out as a target.
explanation.walkthrough: The mark of Cain, from Genesis, is the biblical sign that made him a marked man.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the leader of a team or a ship's commander.

clue.text: Count endless data on card after opening of ballot

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, the only one kept
without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: the first letter of ballot
info is short for information, data
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A returning officer counting votes, with data on cards once the ballot opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb about tallying votes; it is the title of Count Binface, a costumed joke candidate who stands against prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Binface is a satirical candidate with a bin for a head who stood against Sunak in 2024.
